`Spiral.__init__` builds the split order from `main_pane="left"` and `clockwise=True`, so `self.splits` is `["left", "top", "right", "bottom"]`. In `get_spiral`, `main_pane_ratio` is `None`, so every split uses `ratio=0.71`. Starting from `(23, 47, 1621, 941)`, the method repeatedly applies `split_left`, `split_top`, `split_right`, `split_bottom`, cycling directions and carrying forward the remaining rectangle. It appends each produced window until a candidate split would fail `has_invalid_size`, which checks the rectangle against margins `[9, 14, 6, 12]` and `border_width=4`; at that point it appends the current unsplit rectangle and stops. Working through those integer splits yields the seven returned rectangles below.
